primary_work.title: Causal Representation Learning Made Identifiable by Grouping of Observational Variables

decision: NARROWED BEYOND GROUPED-OBSERVATION CRL IDENTIFIABILITY — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: causal representations can be identifiable from supplied grouping of observational variables without temporal structure, interventions, weak supervision, or language under the paper assumptions
known modality, field, parser-slot, or observation grouping is an existing identifiability signal rather than discovery of raw-language equivalence
perfect grouped-observation CRL does not identify within-group utterance classes or semantic target denotation
task success and latent recovery cannot substitute for direct recovery of utterance and target partitions
counterexample: Two models related by simultaneous relabeling of supplied observation groups, recovered latent coordinates, target blocks, raw-utterance classes, denotation, language encoder, decoder, and policy preserve the complete grouped observation law, G-CaRL objective, latent recovery, transition and task metrics, and language-conditioned predictions while assigning different utterance equivalence classes and semantic target correspondences.
official_code_status: paper-specific official code verified; only Python3 and PyTorch are documented, with no dependency lock, release, three-seed manifest, checksums, or R0 resource bundle
